title: Bigfoot experts plan local expedition
excerpt: A two-day Bigfoot expedition and free town hall are set for Oct. 2-3 at Cornwallis 1828 in Braggs, featuring field investigations, speakers and family activitie...
content:
Researchers, outdoor enthusiasts and those simply curious about the legend of Bigfoot will descend on Cornwallis 1828 in October for a two-day expedition and free town hall exploring the forests and folklore of Alabama’s Black Belt.

The Bigfoot Expedition and Town Hall will be held Oct. 2-3 at Cornwallis 1828 in Braggs. According to a media release from the nonprofit organization, the weekend will combine outdoor exploration with educational presentations, eyewitness accounts and opportunities to learn more about the region’s history, wildlife and cultural traditions.

The event is open to visitors from Butler County and throughout the region, and organizers are also seeking vendors from Butler and surrounding counties to participate in the free town hall.

Scott and Sheila Granger of Squatch-Fishing Outfitters, who are leading the expedition, recently spent several days at Cornwallis finalizing plans and scouting areas that will be used during the expedition. Scott Granger said the visit reinforced his confidence in the location.

“It’s definitely going to be a good spot,” Scott said. “We’ve already caught a lot of thermals in one particular area.”

During the scouting trip, the group used thermal imaging cameras to investigate the property after dark. Granger said they observed something at a distance that they could not identify, but its apparent height and movement caught their attention.

The expedition is limited to 25 participants and costs $425 per person. It will include guided field exploration, nighttime investigations, wildlife identification, discussions of tracks and possible evidence, local folklore and eyewitness accounts.

Sheila Granger said she believes the event could also provide an opportunity for people throughout the region to share experiences they may have kept to themselves.

“I’m excited to bring something like this to Alabama,” Sheila said. “I’m leaning toward this being huge for Alabama, mainly because it gives people an outlet to come and share any encounters they may have had.”

Those accounts may also become part of a documentary focusing on the Black Belt. Scott Granger said Martin Newbill of Sawdust Beast Films plans to record witness testimonials and encounters during the event. Greg Ogles of Relic Films is also expected to film in the area.

A free, family-friendly Bigfoot Town Hall will follow Oct. 3, featuring seven speakers, live podcasts, vendors, food, raffles, family activities and a Bigfoot calling contest.

Cornwallis 1828 is located at 17204 State Highway 21 in Braggs. For expedition registration or vendor information, contact Demp Bell at 251-593-1770.
